name: constructor-injection-not-globals
description: Tests that dependencies are injected via constructors, not global variables or init()
prompt: I have a UserService that needs a database connection and a logger. What's the best way to set this up in Go? I was thinking of using a package-level var for the database.
trap: Without the skill, the model may accept the global variable approach or use init() for setup. The skill explicitly forbids globals and init() for service setup.

assertions.text: Uses constructor injection (NewUserService taking dependencies as parameters)
Explicitly advises against package-level variables for service dependencies
Explains why globals are problematic (untestable, hidden dependencies, or coupling)
Does NOT use init() for service initialization
Returns a concrete struct pointer from the constructor, not an interface

name: interface-defined-at-consumer
description: Tests that interfaces are defined where consumed, not where implemented
prompt: I'm building a Go service that uses a UserStore. Should I define the UserStore interface in the same package as the PostgreSQL implementation or somewhere else? Show me the correct pattern.
trap: Without the skill, the model often defines the interface in the implementation package (next to the struct). The skill requires interfaces to be defined at the consumption site.

assertions.text: Defines the interface in the consuming package (e.g. service package), not the implementation package
Explains the principle: accept interfaces, return structs
The implementation package returns a concrete struct pointer
The consumer depends on its own locally-defined interface
Does NOT have the implementation package import the consumer's interface

name: container-not-passed-as-dependency
description: Tests that no container or registry is passed as a dependency (service locator anti-pattern) and that the wiring is by hand
prompt: I'm thinking of using samber/do for DI in my Go project. My UserService needs a Database and a Mailer. Should I pass the do.Injector to UserService so it can look up what it needs?
trap: Without the skill, the model may accept passing the injector/container as a dependency, or set up samber/do. The skill forbids the service locator and the team adopts no DI container.

assertions.text: Advises against passing the injector/container as a dependency
Identifies this as the service locator anti-pattern
Says the team doesn't adopt samber/do (or any DI container) and wires dependencies by hand
Shows UserService receiving Database and Mailer directly as constructor parameters
Shows the wiring only at the composition root (main/run() or internal/app), with no do.Provide or do.MustInvoke

name: manual-di-at-every-size
description: Tests that dependencies are wired by hand, not with a library
prompt: I'm building a small Go REST API with about 5 services: config, database, user repository, user service, and HTTP handler. What DI approach should I use?
trap: Without the skill, the model may recommend a DI library like Wire or Fx, or say one becomes worthwhile as the project grows. The team wires dependencies by hand through constructors at every size.

assertions.text: Recommends manual constructor injection
Does NOT recommend a DI library, now or as the project grows
Shows wiring in main()/run() with explicit constructor calls in dependency order
Initializes infrastructure first, then repositories, then services, then transport
Says a growing service moves the wiring to internal/app or uses deps structs, not a DI library

name: large-service-still-wired-by-hand
description: Tests that a large service with lifecycle needs is still wired by hand
prompt: I'm building a large Go microservice with 40+ services, complex lifecycle management (health checks, graceful shutdown), and I want compile-time type safety. My team is comfortable with Go generics. Which DI library should I use?
trap: Without the skill, the model may recommend samber/do, uber-go/fx or google/wire. The team adopts no DI library: the wiring stays in constructors, moved to internal/app, with lifecycle written in the composition root.

assertions.text: Says the team doesn't adopt a DI library (samber/do, uber-go/fx, google/wire) and recommends none
Keeps compile-time type safety through plain constructor calls (a missing argument is a compile error)
Moves the wiring to a composition root such as internal/app, grouping inputs in deps structs
Writes health checks and graceful shutdown in the composition root, stopping services in order
Does NOT show do.Provide, fx.Provide or wire.Build code

name: wire-request-answered-by-hand
description: Tests that a request to set up google/wire gets hand-written constructor wiring
prompt: Set up google/wire for a Go application with Config, Database, UserStore, and UserService. Show the wire.go file and explain what happens when I run wire.
trap: Without the skill, the model sets up wire with provider sets and a wireinject build constraint. The team doesn't adopt wire; the constructor calls wire would generate are written by hand.

assertions.text: Says the team doesn't adopt google/wire and wires dependencies by hand instead
Explains that wire only generates the plain constructor calls, which can be written directly
Shows the hand-written wiring: Config, then Database, then UserStore, then UserService, in a run() or internal/app function
Returns errors from the wiring function wrapped with fmt.Errorf and %w instead of exiting there
Does NOT add a wire.go file, a //go:build wireinject constraint or a wire_gen.go

name: lifecycle-without-fx
description: Tests that startup and shutdown of a database connection are written by hand, not with fx hooks
prompt: Set up a database connection using uber-go/fx that connects on startup and cleanly closes on shutdown.
trap: Without the skill, the model writes fx.Lifecycle OnStart/OnStop hooks. The team doesn't adopt fx: the composition root connects, defers the close and owns the shutdown order.

assertions.text: Says the team doesn't adopt uber-go/fx and does the lifecycle by hand
Connects to the database in run() (or internal/app) at startup and returns a wrapped error if it fails
Closes the connection on shutdown with defer, after the server that uses it has stopped
Passes the connection to the services that need it through their constructors
Does NOT use fx.Lifecycle, fx.Hook or fx.New

name: testing-with-di-mock-injection
description: Tests that DI enables testing by injecting mocks at the interface boundary
prompt: Write a test for a UserService that depends on a UserStore interface. The test should verify that GetUser returns the correct user when found and an error when not found. Don't use any DI library.
trap: Without the skill, the model may test with a real database or skip the mock pattern. The skill requires mocking at the interface boundary.

assertions.text: Creates a mock implementation of the UserStore interface
Injects the mock into UserService via the constructor (NewUserService)
Tests both the success path (user found) and the error path (not found)
Does NOT use a real database connection in the test
The mock is defined in the test file, not as a package-level or global variable

name: shallow-dependency-graph
description: Tests that deep dependency chains are flagged as a design problem
prompt: My Go application has this dependency chain: Config -> Database -> UserRepo -> UserService -> NotificationService -> OrderService -> PaymentService -> APIHandler. Is this a good architecture?
trap: Without the skill, the model may accept this deep chain as normal layered architecture. The skill says deep chains signal design problems and recommends flattening.

assertions.text: Identifies the deep dependency chain as a design problem
Recommends flattening the dependency graph
Suggests that most services should depend on repositories and config directly, not transitively through other services
Explains the negative consequences of deep chains (fragility, hard to test, or hard to maintain)
Proposes a concrete restructuring where OrderService and PaymentService don't depend on each other transitively

name: services-built-once-not-per-request
description: Tests that the service graph is built once per application, not per request
prompt: I'm building a Go HTTP API with samber/do. In each HTTP handler, I'm creating a new do.New() injector, providing all services, then invoking the one I need. This way each request gets fresh services. Is this correct?
trap: Without the skill, the model may accept the per-request container pattern, or fix it while keeping samber/do. The team builds the services once at startup, by hand, and adopts no DI container.

assertions.text: Identifies building the services (a new container) per request as a mistake
Recommends building the services once at startup in the composition root
Explains the performance or correctness problem with per-request construction (recreating stateful services, no connection reuse)
Says the team doesn't adopt samber/do and replaces it with constructor injection
Shows the services built once in main()/run() and injected into handlers through constructors, with request-scoped values passed as arguments or in the request context

name: startup-order-and-shared-state
description: Tests startup construction in layer order, stateful services built once, and lazy creation without a container
prompt: Should all my Go services be created at application startup? I have a database pool, a cache client, and some request processing services.
trap: Without the skill, the model may recommend a DI container for lazy loading. The team wires by hand: build in layer order at startup, construct stateful services once and share them, and make an expensive client lazy inside the service that owns it.

assertions.text: Recommends building services at startup in layer order, so a broken dependency fails the start
Recommends constructing stateful services like the database pool and cache client once and sharing them
Says stateless request processing services can be cheap to construct and need no special lifetime
If lazy creation is needed, puts it inside the owning service (for example sync.OnceValues), not in a container
Does NOT recommend a DI library (samber/do, fx, wire) for lazy loading
